card.name: Words just before a noun like product or type
card.fires_on: Words in drug-label dosing text where a noun such as product, type, form or component is likely next, e.g. the end of a drug name, "insulin" in "insulin naïve", or a comma after NSAIDs.

modes.label: End of drug name
modes.description: The last piece of a drug name before a word like product or component.
modes.example: Use another venlafax<<ine>> extended-release product for dosage initiation

modes.label: Insulin as modifier
modes.description: The word insulin before naïve or in the phrase any other insulin.
modes.example: Do not mix HUMALOG U-200 with any other<< insulin>>.

modes.label: Linking word in dosing phrases
modes.description: A small word or comma in a dosing or composition phrase where a category noun is expected next.

card.writes: It promotes words like type and types and suppresses ingredient and powder words, so it favors a category noun over a substance noun.
card.plain: It fires where the label is about to name a kind or type of product rather than an ingredient.
